groups.title: The models represent the contract behaviour correctly.

parts.A-SOURCE-SHAPED: We assume the handwritten Lean models represent the Solidity behaviour described by this guarantee.
parts.A-ABSTRACT-TX: The model defines transaction success and failure without executing EVM bytecode.
parts.A-VERITY-SCAFFOLD: We also assume Verity correctly models the calls, storage and rollback used by these proofs.
parts.A-CLASSICAL-CHOICE: Lean proofs may use classical choice alongside propext and Quot.sound; these foundational axioms remain visible in Trust output.
parts.A-NO-REENTRY: External calls are assumed to preserve protected storage and balances and reject re-entry. This includes user-selected withdrawal recipients and per-call consolidation refund recipients; their bodies are not proved.

groups.mitigation: Source-shaped paths: differential tests cover selected executions. Verity: a pinned dependency and recomputed axiom audit detect dependency drift and proof escapes. Abstract rollback and arbitrary-recipient storage preservation have no general mitigation here; they remain explicit premises.

groups.title: The deployed contracts correspond to the source we reviewed.

parts.A-SOLC-TRUSTED: We assume the compiler and compilation pipeline preserve the source behaviour.
parts.A-RUNTIME-PROVENANCE: We assume the deployed contracts and proxy implementations correspond to the pinned source.
parts.A-SUPPORTED-MODULES: Each module is assumed to satisfy the NOR-style counter representation, admitted history and explicit arithmetic bounds. This is not proved for NOR, CSM or CuratedModuleV2; the last two are outside the pinned core source.

groups.mitigation: Recorded runtime hashes and library links are checked. General source-to-runtime correspondence remains open, including the PausableUntil.sol difference documented in PROVENANCE.md. Module registration is role-restricted; that does not prove module invariants.

groups.title: Hashing and transported build evidence have explicit trust boundaries.

parts.A-SHA256-FFI: SHA-256 behavior comes from an opaque FFI/precompile interface; structural SSZ proofs do not prove the hash implementation correct.
parts.A-MULTI-NODE-TRANSPORT: Remote build receipts require exact source and toolchain identity checks; a successful job is not an independent audit.
parts.A-EIP4788-AUTHENTIC: We assume the BEACON_ROOTS reply is the authentic EIP-4788 beacon root for the requested timestamp; the history-ring implementation is not proved.

groups.mitigation: Transport: local rebuilds and hashed logs bind evidence to source and toolchain. Hashing: Solidity uses Ethereum’s SHA-256 precompile; its correspondence to the proof oracle is assumed. Beacon roots: the canonical system contract restricts writes and checks timestamps; its history implementation is not proved here.
